title: The S3 VGA, system control and extension registers
covers: The S3 registers reached through the CRT controller index at hex 03D4 and its data port at hex 03D5, with the sequencer and attribute ports they share

rows.text: The CRT controller registers are reached through the index at 3?4H and the data port at 3?5H; 3BX or 3DX follows bit 0 of the Miscellaneous Output register at 3C2H.
The index at 3?4H also selects the S3 VGA registers, the system control registers and the system extension registers.
The index register at 3?4H is loaded with a binary value, bits 7-0, that indexes the CRT controller register to access.
A write to the data register stores its byte in the CRT controller register the index names.
The data register is readable and returns the byte of the indexed register.
DOSBox-X installs SVGA_S3_WriteCRTC and SVGA_S3_ReadCRTC as the hooks of this port.
A write to index 18H also sets the low eight bits of the shared line-compare state to the byte.
The sequencer is reached by writing an index to 3C4H, then reading or writing the data register at 3C5H.
The data register at 3C5H is the port for the sequencer register the index names; bits 7-0 carry its data.
The index register at 3C4H holds bits 2-0 as the sequencer address and bits 7-3 reserved zero.
A write stores a byte in the indexed sequencer register; the port is read/write.
DOSBox-X installs SVGA_S3_WriteSEQ and SVGA_S3_ReadSEQ as the hooks of this port.
The attribute index and data registers share address 3C0H for writes, selected by an internal address flip-flop.
A write loads bits 4-0 as the attribute index, sets bit 5 to enable palette video and leaves bits 7-6 reserved.
DOSBox-X installs no S3-specific write hook here; the standard VGA attribute controller handles the port.
The attribute controller data register is read at 3C1H and written through 3C0H; it carries the data of the attribute register the index names.
A read at 3C1H returns the byte of the indexed attribute register; bits 7-0 are that data.
DOSBox-X installs no S3-specific read hook on 3C1H; the standard attribute controller returns the indexed register.
The 86C928 gives one description for indices 24H and 26H: read-only registers returning the attribute index and its address flip-flop.
Bits 5-0 are the attribute index, bit 6 is reserved zero and bit 7 is the inverted address flip-flop.
DOSBox-X returns the low five bits of the attribute index and sets bit 5 when the palette is enabled; bit 7 reads 0.
CR30 is read-only at index 30H and reports the chip ID and revision status; the 86C928 book gives 90H as its default.
A read at index 30H returns the chip ID and revision status byte.
The Trio book gives CR30 default E1H and says an E in the upper nibble means to use CR2D-CR2F for the chip ID.
DOSBox-X returns E1H for Trio32 or later, C0H for Vision864 or later, B0H on PCI 86C928 and 90H on ISA or EISA.
CR31 is read/write at index 31H, default 00H, holding CPUA BASE, SCRN 2.PG, VGA 16B, ENH MAP, start address bits 17-16, font fetch and BIOS mapping.
A write stores bits 0-2: CPUA BASE, SCRN 2.PG and VGA 16B.
A write stores bit 3, which forces enhanced memory mapping.
A write stores bits 5-4 as start address bits 17-16; CR51 bit 2 adds bit 18.
A write stores bit 6 as page-mode font fetch and bit 7 as the external BIOS mapping of C6000H-C67FFFH, which strapping PD3 overrides.
A write also derives chain-4 from bit 3 and re-evaluates the mode and the handlers.
CR35 at index 35H, default 00H, holds CPU base address bits 17-14 in bits 3-0 and two lock bits.
A write stores bits 3-0 as the CPU address base in 64K units and bit 4 to lock the vertical timing registers.
Bit 4 locks CR06, CR07, CR09 bit 5, CR10, CR11 bits 3-0, CR15 and CR16; bit 5 locks CR00-CR05 and CR17 bit 2; bits 7-6 are reserved.
A write is ignored unless CR38 holds 48H; it stores only bits 7-4, and bits 3-0 become the read and write bank numbers.
A read returns the stored high nibble or'ed with the current bank number.
CR2D is read-only at index 2DH and should hold the upper byte of the PCI device ID; the capture prints its default as SSH.
A read returns the chip ID high byte in bits 7-0.
CR2E is read-only at index 2EH; its default is 10H for a Trio32 and 11H for a Trio64, letting software tell them apart.
A read returns the chip ID low byte: 10H for a Trio32 or 11H for a Trio64.
CR2F is read-only at index 2FH and reports the revision level; the book gives its default in the description.
A read returns the revision level in bits 7-0.
Indices 36H and 37H are read-only and sample the reset state of the PD bus pins 15-0; their default depends on strapping.
Bits 1-0 name the system bus and bit 2 gives the VGA ROM data bus width.
Bit 3 disables or enables the C6000H-C67FFFH part of the C0000H-C7FFFH BIOS ROM area, and bit 4 selects the MEMCS16 address range.
Bits 7-5 give the display memory size: 000 4 MB, 010 3 MB, 100 2 MB, 110 1 MB and 111 0.5 MB.
Bit 8 selects the subsystem setup source or the 86C805, bit 9 is always 1 and bit 10 extends the monitor ID.
Bit 11 controls NOWS or LOCA, bit 12 MEMCS16 or the DAC LOCA, and bits 15-13 identify the monitor type.
DOSBox-X builds CR36 from the memory size and fast-page mode, not the strapping pins, and returns the constant 2BH for CR37.
CR38 is read/write at index 38H, default 00H; loading 01xx10xx unlocks the S3 register set.
A write stores the lock byte; a pattern 01xx10xx unlocks the S3 registers.
DOSBox-X stores the whole byte, and CR35's write proceeds only when the lock equals 48H, not any 01xx10xx.
CR39 is read/write at index 39H, default 00H; loading 101xxxxx unlocks the system control and extension registers.
A write stores the lock byte; 101xxxxx unlocks the system control and system extension registers.
DOSBox-X stores the byte in reg_lock2 and its read returns it; the write case does nothing else, so the 101xxxxx pattern unlocks nothing.
CR3A is read/write at 3B?H index 3AH, default printed as DOH, holding refresh control, top-of-memory, the 256-colour mode, fast font writing and MEMCS16.
A write stores bits 1-0 as the refresh count and bit 2 as the enable of that alternate count.
A write stores bit 3 for top-of-memory access, bit 4 for the 256-colour mode and bit 5 for high-speed font writing.
A write stores bit 6 as reserved zero and bit 7 as the MEMCS16 enable.
CR40 is read/write at index 40H, default A4H, holding EN-A 8514, SIG SEL, WST CTL, EWRT POST, DEC-WAIT and RD-WAIT.
A write stores bit 0 for enhanced register access and bit 1 for the MIDO/MID1 or STRD/BGNT/BREQ signals.
A write stores bit 2 for one wait state and bit 3 for the fast write buffer.
A write stores bits 5-4 as the decode wait states and bits 7-6 as the read wait states.
CR41 is read/write at index 41H, default 00H; it is a BIOS flag register and users should not write to it.
A write stores the byte of BIOS-FLAG-REGISTER-1.
CR42 is read/write at index 42H, default 00H, holding the dot clock select, an interlaced mode bit and reserved bits.
A write stores bits 3-0 as the dot clock select, effective when the VGA clock select is 11; the table gives example frequencies.
A write stores bit 5 as interlaced mode; bits 4 and 7-6 are reserved.
The mode control register is readable.
A read returns the constant 0DH, not the stored byte.
A write triggers a resize when bit 5 changes.
CR43 is read/write at index 43H, default 00H, holding the clock edge, DAC RS2, screen width bit 8, 16-bit colour, XEN and counter double bits.
A write stores bit 0 for both clock edges and bit 1 as DAC register select bit 2, disabled unless CR55 bits 3-2 are 0,0.
A write stores bit 2 as screen width bit 8, disabled unless CR51 bits 5-4 are 0,0, and bit 3 as 16-bit colour mode.
A write stores bit 4 to move the X2E8H port to X148H, bits 6-5 reserved and bit 7 for horizontal counter doubling.
Bit 2 is not kept in reg_43: it is stored as bit 8 of the scan length and read back from there.
CR45 is read/write at index 45H, default 00H, holding the hardware cursor enable, two stretch bits, right storage, the Bt485 enable and reserved bits.
A write stores bit 0 to enable the hardware graphics cursor in enhanced mode; bit 1 is reserved.
A write stores bit 2 for twice width with stack pointers 0-1 and bit 3 for triple width with pointers 0-2.
A write stores bit 4 for cursor storage in the last bytes of each line, at 4 or 8 bits per pixel.
A write stores bit 5 for the Bt485 ODF/CDE signals, effective only with CR55 bit 5; bits 7-6 are reserved.
The cursor mode register is readable.
A read returns the stored mode or'ed with A0H and resets both cursor stack pointers.
Indices 46H and 47H hold the cursor origin X; the high three bits go to CR46 and the low byte to CR47.
A write stores the X coordinate of the cursor left side, bits 10-0; bits 15-11 are reserved.
DOSBox-X takes all eight bits of CR46 as originx bits 15-8, where the document keeps three.
Indices 48H and 49H hold the cursor origin Y; the high three bits go to CR48 and the low byte to CR49.
A write stores the Y coordinate, bits 10-0, and registers the cursor X and Y position when the high byte is written.
DOSBox-X takes all eight bits of CR48 as originy bits 15-8 and registers nothing on the high-byte write.
CR4A stacks three true-colour foreground registers; reading CR45 resets the pointer and each write increments it, giving 24 bits in three writes.
A write stores one byte at the current stack pointer and increments it.
The register is read/write.
A write past the third stack entry wraps the pointer to 0.
CR4B stacks three true-colour background registers; reading CR45 resets the pointer and each write increments it, giving 24 bits in three writes.
A write stores one byte at the current stack pointer and increments it.
The register is read/write.
A write past the third stack entry wraps the pointer to 0.
CR4C and CR4D are read/write at indexes 4CH and 4DH, default undefined; they hold bits 11-0 of the cursor storage start address and bits 15-12 are reserved.
A write stores the value's high four bits in CR4C and its low byte in CR4D.
Both registers are readable.
A start address that would run past the end of video memory is reduced to its low byte and a warning is logged.
A read of index 4CH or 4DH returns 00H from the switch's default arm, not the stored address.
CR4E is read/write at index 4EH, default undefined; bits 5-0 are the pattern display start X pixel position and bits 7-6 are reserved.
A write stores bits 5-0 as the display start X position.
The register is readable.
A read of index 4EH returns 00H from the switch's default arm, not the stored position.
CR4F is read/write at index 4FH, default undefined; bits 5-0 are the pattern display start Y pixel position and bits 7-6 are reserved.
A write stores bits 5-0 as the display start Y position.
The register is readable.
A read of index 4FH returns 00H from the switch's default arm, not the stored position.
CR50 is read/write at index 50H with power-on default 00H.
A write stores bit 2, which enables the BREQ and BGNT functions.
A write stores bit 3, which disables the LOCA/SRDY signals.
A write stores bits 5-4, which select the pixel length for graphics engine commands: 1, 2 or 4 bytes.
A write stores bits 7-6, which select the engine command screen pixel width: 1024/2048, 640, 800 or 1280.
Bits 1-0 are reserved.
The register is readable.
A write stores the byte, then sets the XGA colour mode from bits 5-4: 8, 16 or 32 bpp, and 4 bpp when CR67's high nibble is FH.
A write sets 1024, 640, 800 or 1280 from bits 7-6 and also reads bit 0: 01H gives 1152, 81H gives 1600, 41H and C1H give 1024.
CR51 is read/write at index 51H with power-on default 00H.
A write stores bits 1-0 as display start address bits 19-18, extension bits of CR31 bits 5-4.
A write stores bits 3-2 as CPU base address bits 19-18, extension bits of CR35 bits 3-0.
A write stores bits 5-4 as logical screen width bits 9-8, extension bits of CR13.
A non-zero value in bits 5-4 disables CR43 bit 2.
A write stores bit 6, which disables split transfers.
A write stores bit 7, which enables EPROM write control to the BIOS ROM address.
The register is readable.
A write that changes bits 2-3 rebuilds the memory handlers and one that changes bits 4-5 rechecks the scan length.
A write to CR43 still sets or clears scan length bit 8, so the disable is not applied.
CR52 is read/write at index 52H, default 00H; it is a BIOS flag register and users should not write to it.
A write stores the BIOS flag byte.
The register is readable.
CR53 is read/write at index 53H with power-on default 00H.
Bits 3-0 enable write-per-bit flags for each 1MB memory bank.
Bit 4 enables MMIO access.
Bit 5 selects parallel VRAM addressing.
Bit 6 swaps nibbles in each byte of a linear memory address read or write.
Bit 7 enables nibble write control for the graphics engine.
The register is readable.
A write that changes the stored byte rebuilds the memory handlers.
CR55 is read/write at index 55H with power-on default 00H.
Bits 1-0 are DAC register select bits 3-2, and a non-zero value disables CR43 bit 1.
Bit 2 enables the general input port read and disables video DAC reads.
Bit 3 enables external SID operation.
Bit 4 selects the hardware cursor MS/X11 mode.
Bit 5 enables hardware cursor external operation mode.
Bit 6 is reserved.
Bit 7 disables the PA output, tri-stating PA[7:0] and VCLK.
The register is readable.
CR58 is read/write at index 58H with power-on default 00H.
Bits 1-0 select the linear address window size: 64KB, 1MB, 2MB or 4MB.
Bit 2 enables the read-ahead cache.
Bit 3 latches the address during every ISA cycle.
Bit 4 enables linear addressing.
Bit 5 limits the write-post entry depth.
Bit 6 selects 256-word SAM control.
Bit 7 selects a 6-MCLK random read/write cycle time.
The register is readable.
A write starts an update of the linear frame buffer.
CR59 and CR5A are read/write at indexes 59H-5AH with power-on default 000AH.
A write stores the 16-bit window position in 26-bit CPU address space, on a size-aligned boundary that ignores some low bits; bits 15-10 are reserved.
Both registers are readable.
A write stores every bit of the position, applies no boundary alignment and masks no reserved bit; the bytes are read back whole.
CR5D is read/write at index 5DH with power-on default 00H.
Bits 2-0 are bits 8 of the horizontal total, display end and start horizontal blank values.
Bit 3 is reserved.
Bit 4 is bit 8 of the start horizontal sync position.
Bit 5 is reserved.
Bit 6 is bit 8 of the data transfer position and bit 7 bit 8 of the bus-grant terminate position.
The register is readable.
A write that changes bits 0-1 resizes the screen.
CR5E is read/write at index 5EH with power-on default 00H.
Bits 2-0 are bits 10 of the vertical total, vertical display end and start vertical blank values.
Bit 3 is reserved.
Bit 4 is bit 10 of the vertical retrace start.
Bit 5 is reserved.
Bit 6 is bit 10 of the line compare position.
Bit 7 is reserved.
The register is readable.
A write that changes bits 0-1 resizes the screen.
CR63 is read/write at index 63H, default 00H.
A write stores bits 3-0 as the number of character clocks the HSYNC reset is delayed from the master VSYNC falling edge.
A write stores bits 7-4 as the number of DCLKs to delay the character clock reset at the end of the scan line.
Both fields take effect only in remote mode, CR56 bit 0.
The register is readable.
On the 86C928 and Vision boards a write is ignored and a read returns 00H; on a ViRGE a write of bit 1 resets the 3D engine.
CR66 is read/write at index 66H, default 00H.
Bits 5-0 are reserved.
A write stores bit 6, which tri-states the pixel address bus PA[15:0].
A write stores bit 7, which enables PCI bus disconnection.
The register is readable.
On a ViRGE a write of bit 1 resets the 3D engine.
CR67 is read/write at index 67H, default 00H.
A write stores bit 0 as the VCLK phase: clear inverts VCLK with respect to DCLK and set keeps them in phase.
Bits 3-1 are reserved.
A write stores bits 7-4 as the RAMDAC colour mode: 8, 15, 16 or 24 bits per pixel.
The register is readable.
A write also calls the colour-mode update and re-derives the video mode.
CR69 is read/write at index 69H, default 00H.
A write stores bits 3-0 as display start address bits 19-16.
A non-zero value makes CR31 bits 5-4 and CR51 bits 1-0 ignored.
Bits 7-4 are reserved.
The register is readable.
A write also takes bit 4 of the value as bit 20 of the display start address.
A CR31 write still changes display start bits 16-17 and a CR51 write bits 18-19, so the old bits are not ignored.
CR6A is read/write at index 6AH, default 00H.
A write stores bits 5-0 as CPU base address bits 19-14.
A non-zero value makes CR35 bits 3-0 and CR51 bits 3-2 ignored.
Bits 7-6 are reserved.
The register is readable.
A write also takes bit 6 of the value as the bank's bit 6.
A CR35 write still changes the low four bank bits and a CR51 write bits 4-5, so the old bits are not ignored.
CR6B is read/write at index 6BH, default 00H, a flag register reserved for the S3 BIOS.
A write stores the BIOS flag byte.
The register is readable.
SR8 is read/write at index 08H with power-on default 00H.
Loading xxxx0110b, for example 06H, unlocks access to the S3 extended sequencer registers SR9-SR18.
The register is readable.
Writes of any sequencer index above 08H are ignored, and reads of 09H-1AH return 00H, until the value stored here is 06H.
Only 06H unlocks: other xxxx0110b values such as 16H are stored but leave SR9-SR18 locked.
SR10 is read/write at index 10H; with SR11 it gives an MCLK of 45 MHz by default.
Bits 4-0 are the PLL N divider (1-31) and bits 6-5 the PLL R value (1, 2, 4 or 8) scaling the MCLK PLL output.
Bit 7 is reserved.
The register is readable.
A write stores bits 4-0 as N and bits 7-5 as R, so the reserved bit 7 also scales the clock.
SR11 is read/write at index 11H; with SR10 it gives an MCLK of 45 MHz by default.
Bits 6-0 are the PLL M divider (1-127) in the MCLK feedback loop.
Bit 7 is reserved.
The register is readable.
SR12 is read/write at index 12H; with SR13 it gives a DCLK of 25.175 MHz by default.
A new value loads when bit 1 or bit 5 of SR15 is set and bits 3-2 of 3C2H are 11b.
Bits 4-0 are the N divider and bits 6-5 the R value for the DCLK PLL.
Bit 7 is reserved.
The register is readable.
A write stores bits 4-0 as N and bits 7-5 as R, so the reserved bit 7 also scales the clock.
The emulator's own clock setter also writes the N and R values when a VGA mode asks for a frequency.
SR13 is read/write at index 13H; with SR12 it gives a DCLK of 25.175 MHz by default.
Bits 6-0 are the PLL M divider (1-127) in the DCLK feedback loop.
Bit 7 is reserved.
The register is readable.
The emulator's own clock setter also writes the M value when a VGA mode asks for a frequency.
SR15 is read/write at index 15H with power-on default 00H.
A write stores bit 0, which loads the new MCLK frequency and should then be cleared, or bit 5 for an immediate load.
A write stores bit 1, which loads the new DCLK frequency, with bits 3-2 of 3C2H also at 11b.
A write stores bit 2, which outputs the internally generated MCLK on pin 147 for testing.
A write stores bit 3, which makes the VCLK direction follow the EVCLK signal.
A write stores bit 4, which divides DCLK by 2; either it or bit 6 must be set for clock-doubled RAMDAC operation.
A write stores bit 5, which loads the MCLK and DCLK PLL values immediately; the register must never be left set to 1.
A write stores bit 6, which inverts DCLK; either it or bit 4 must be set for clock-doubled RAMDAC operation.
A write stores bit 7, which enables two-cycle memory writes.
The register is readable.
A write also restarts the screen resize.
SR17 is read-only at index 17H, default 00H, and reserved for S3 testing of the clock synthesizer.
A write has no effect.
Once SR8 holds 06H, a read returns 7BH, C0H, 00H and DAH in turn.
